title: Inventory Service Cascading OOMKilled Failure during Flash Sale

impact.user_impact_summary: Users experienced stock lookup timeouts and inventory reservation delays during initial flash sale rush.

five_whys.question: Why did inventory lookups time out?
five_whys.answer: All 4 inventory-service pods entered CrashLoopBackOff due to OOMKilled terminations.

five_whys.question: Why did the pods exceed their memory limits (256Mi)?
five_whys.answer: An in-memory local caching mechanism stored unbounded flash sale item queries without TTL eviction.

five_whys.question: Why was unbounded local caching enabled in inventory-service?
five_whys.answer: The service was originally designed for lower traffic catalogs and had not been refactored to use centralized Redis.

five_whys.question: Why did the HPA (Horizontal Pod Autoscaler) not prevent memory saturation?
five_whys.answer: HPA was configured solely on CPU utilization (75%) rather than memory utilization or custom request rate metrics.

five_whys.question: Why were memory limits set to 256Mi without safety headroom?
five_whys.answer: Resource quotas had not been reviewed since initial cluster provisioning 8 months prior.

what_went_well: Kubelet terminated memory-hogging pods before the node Linux kernel entered global kernel panic.
HPA scaled replicas from 4 to 12 once memory limits were raised to 1Gi.
what_went_poorly: Lack of Redis-backed distributed cache created single-pod hotspots.
HPA metric was blind to memory saturation.
where_we_got_lucky: Flash sale marketing campaign peaked in stages, preventing total cascading crash of payment-gateway.

action_items.description: Migrate in-memory catalog cache to centralized Redis cluster with strict LRU eviction.
Configure Prometheus HPA to scale on both CPU (>70%) and Memory (>75%) utilization.
